note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Shared low-rank subspace limits LoRA; U-LoRA's gating design and its empirical validation

nodes.name: Vanilla LoRA shares one subspace
nodes.description: In vanilla LoRA, parameter updates are constrained to a fixed-rank low-dimensional subspace shared across all input contexts, causing interference among updates for different semantic contexts.

nodes.name: Same token needs different directions
nodes.description: The same token (e.g. 'book') can take different semantic roles across tasks, yet vanilla LoRA reuses highly similar low-rank update directions because of its shared bases.

nodes.name: Input-aware LoRA is uncoordinated
nodes.description: Input-aware LoRA variants (LoRA-MoE, HydraLoRA, TopLoRA) select low-rank directions per token independently, producing dispersed, uncoordinated updates within the same sentence or task and weak task-level consistency.

nodes.name: U-LoRA token-wise gating
nodes.description: U-LoRA replaces LoRA's constant down-projection A with A(x)=G(x)⊙A, where an input-conditioned gate modulates the shared low-rank bases element-wise per token; G(x)≡1 recovers vanilla LoRA and the update stays within the rank-r subspace.

nodes.name: Sequence-level aggregation
nodes.description: U-LoRA aggregates token features into a softmax-weighted sequence-level directional summary (causally masked in decoder-only models) and adds it to the token-level signal, coordinating utilization within a sentence.

nodes.name: EMA historical prior
nodes.description: U-LoRA calibrates the gate with a bias-corrected exponential moving average of batch-mean sequence summaries, reducing batch-to-batch gate noise; it is training-time only and frozen at inference.

nodes.name: U-LoRA wins on math reasoning
nodes.description: On Gemma-7B, LLaMA-3-8B, Qwen3-8B and Qwen2.5-14B, U-LoRA achieves the best average accuracy on the math reasoning benchmark, e.g. 76.02% (r=8) on LLaMA-3-8B vs 71.67% for LoRA r=32.

nodes.name: U-LoRA wins on GLUE
nodes.description: On GLUE, U-LoRA gets the best average: 84.88%/85.00% (r=8/16) on RoBERTa-Base and 88.13%/88.29% on RoBERTa-Large, above TopLoRA r=16 (84.48%) and LoRA r=32 (83.60%) on Base.

nodes.name: Gains come from utilization, not parameters
nodes.description: Increasing LoRA rank from 16 to 32 gives only marginal gains (82.82 to 83.60 on RoBERTa-Base), while U-LoRA at r=8 matches higher-rank LoRA, so improvements stem from better use of a fixed rank budget.

nodes.name: All three components contribute
nodes.description: Ablation on Qwen3-8B shows removing TOK, SEQ or EMA lowers average accuracy from 83.97 to 78.95, 79.16 and 79.66 respectively, and removing all three gives 78.52, equal to LoRA.

nodes.name: Consistent across ranks and modules
nodes.description: U-LoRA outperforms LoRA at every tested rank in {2,4,8,16,32} and across target-module sets from Q to QKVOGUD on Qwen3-8B.

nodes.name: Task-structured update geometry
nodes.description: PCA of RoBERTa-Large updates shows U-LoRA forms the most compact, well-structured task clusters in deeper layers, while TopLoRA updates are scattered without clear clustering.

isolated_nodes.name: Larger gains on harder reasoning
isolated_nodes.description: On Qwen3-8B, U-LoRA reaches 85.29 on GSM8K vs 75.21 for LoRA r=32 and 43.31 on AQuA vs 36.61.

isolated_nodes.name: CoLA gains
isolated_nodes.description: On CoLA, U-LoRA scores 60.61 (Base) and 66.51 (Large) vs 58.58 and 60.90 for LoRA r=32.

isolated_nodes.name: Effective at 72B and on instruct models
isolated_nodes.description: U-LoRA remains effective at 72B scale and on instruct-tuned models, e.g. +3.24 over TopLoRA on 14B-Instruct.

isolated_nodes.name: SEQ matters for AQuA
isolated_nodes.description: Removing sequence-level aggregation causes particularly severe degradation on AQuA.

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from the shared-subspace limitation of LoRA, through U-LoRA's gating, aggregation and EMA design, to benchmark and ablation evidence.
